basics.name: Prerna Radhakrishna
basics.label: PhD Scholar
basics.summary: I am a PhD researcher studying the cognitive and computational mechanisms underlying curiosity and its effects on memory encoding. My work addresses three interrelated questions: how curiosity — as a motivational state — selectively enhances what we remember; how uncertainty and information gaps drive information-seeking behaviour; and how curiosity modulates learning across contexts. I approach these questions using a combination of behavioural experiments, Bayesian hierarchical modelling, and formal computational frameworks, including information-theoretic and reinforcement learning accounts of curiosity. My meta-analytic work has established that state curiosity reliably benefits memory, and my ongoing experimental work examines the boundary conditions of this effect — including the role of cognitive load, confidence, and prior knowledge — using preregistered multi-session designs. I am interested in developing process-level models that can account for both the motivational and mnemonic signatures of curiosity.

publications.name: Mnemonic benefits of state curiosity — A meta-analysis
